article:
The red text is the teacher

When it breaks, the program is trying to tell you why. Read it. Copy it. Paste it back. Do not start a new chat. Do not delete the project. Do not decide you are “not technical.” The people who look technical are the ones who kept the error.

Debug means: make the failure smaller until you can point at one line. Safety means: the failure should not spend money, leak a key, or mail a thousand people.

A short list that prevents funerals

No live keys in the repo. No agent that can charge. No email blast from a thread you have not read. Test mode until the button has worked twice. Logs you can actually open. A way to turn the thing off.

If you cannot turn it off, you do not run it overnight.

How I actually do it

404s taught more than the pages that worked. /vibe-coding did not exist until it was a real file. The apex domain served the old well while www served the new house. The first save did not push because the token was missing. Each of those was an error with a name. Each one became a line in a lesson.

Where noobs get stuck

Shame. Closing the tab. Or the other shame: pushing forward while the error is still there and hoping the next feature hides it. Errors do not hide. They wait for a stranger.

Film this

A real 404. A real missing env var. Fix both on camera. No soundtrack. End on the page working and the sentence: paste it back.

Do this before chapter 19

  • Break a page on purpose. Fix it from the error alone.
  • Search the repo for the word key. Clean what you find.
  • Write how you would turn the product off at 2am.

Next: shipping in public — a date, a URL, ugly allowed.
